subject: electric eel
title: Electric Eels Were Supposed to Hunt Alone. Then 100 Showed Up

scenes.text: One electric eel gives 860 volts. Ten at once is a different story.
Scientists long believed electric eels always hunted alone.
Then, in a lake beside Brazil's Iriri River, researchers filmed more than a hundred hunting together.
They swim in a circle, herding small fish into a tight ball in shallow water.
Then up to ten eels break off and strike the ball at the same moment.
Ten eels, up to 8,600 volts, and the fish never stood a chance.

description:
Volta's electric eel was thought to be a lone hunter, until researchers filmed groups of more than 100 hunting together in a small lake by the Iriri River in Brazil (Bastos et al., Ecology and Evolution, 2021).
The eels herd tetras into a tight ball, then two to ten of them strike at once. One eel can discharge about 860 volts, so ten could add up to roughly 8,600.
Which animal teamwork surprised you most?
first_comment: Would you rather swim past one electric eel or a hundred that are already busy hunting?
